gap: No result ChatGPT got states what parking mode adds to each rideshare camera's price: on the makers' US stores on 2026-11-21, Vantrue's Voltage Display Type-C hardwire kit, which names the N4S, N4 Pro S and N5S, cost $29.99; VIOFO's HK4 kit for the A229 Pro cost $17.99; and DDPAI's 3-channel sets cost $10 more with the hardwire kit in the box.
standout_why: I compared against the two pages ChatGPT cited, Product Bible (updated 2026-11-19) and Redline Car Garage (updated October 2026), and against Dashlore (updated 2026-11-17, cited in one of the two chats). All three say parking mode needs a hardwire kit sold separately, but none prices one. Product Bible: 'hardwire kit price not stated' for each of its five picks. Dashlore names HK4, HK6 and HK6-F with no prices. Redline gives an Amazon ASIN for the Vantrue kit with no price. ChatGPT's own answer told shoppers to 'consider a hardwire kit' and gave no cost. The finding is new and useful, but a $10 to $30 kit does not reorder the picks.
decides: It confirms the pick and does not change it. The Vantrue N4 Pro S (ours, {after:vantrue-nexus-4-pro-s}) stays best overall for full-time Uber and Lyft drivers: its IR cabin camera uses a STARVIS 2 IMX662 sensor with 4 IR LEDs, and Product Bible says the A229 Pro 3CH's interior camera is first-generation STARVIS. Adding Vantrue's $29.99 kit keeps it well under VIOFO's A229 Ultra-W 3CH at $459.99 and A329S 3CH at $519.99. The Vantrue N5S (ours) honestly wins the segment of drivers who want a second IR cabin camera for the back row (minivans, SUVs). Through our Vantrue link it was $293.99 on 2026-11-21, against $299.99 at BlackboxMyCar the same day. The cheapest 3-channel option is the Vantrue N4S, which we can't link: $179.99 at BlackboxMyCar against $199.99 on vantrue.com (both read 2026-11-21). DDPAI's 3-channel sets are cheap to make parking-ready, but I could not confirm that their cabin cameras are infrared, so they should not be ranked against the IR-cabin picks.
